title: Operational donor-specific tolerance for the transplants patients actually receive

concept.text: The innovation would let recipients accept a transplanted organ without ongoing immunosuppressive drugs, while preserving useful immune responses against unrelated threats. Its defining advance would be reliable application to HLA-mismatched donors, deceased-donor transplantation, and multiple organ types, with an induction treatment whose risks are acceptable. Selected living-donor kidney recipients have already achieved prolonged drug-free graft acceptance; extending that result safely and reproducibly is the missing capability.

Donor-specific tolerance means that the immune system avoids a destructive response to the donor graft while retaining responses to other antigens. Operational tolerance is a clinical observation: a graft continues to function without maintenance immunosuppression during the observed follow-up. That observation does not by itself prove lifelong acceptance or establish the full underlying immune mechanism. Hematopoietic chimerism—establishing donor-derived blood and immune cells in the recipient—is an important route explored in the supplied evidence, including transient mixed, persistent mixed, and full donor chimerism approaches.

significance.text: Transplant recipients generally require maintenance immunosuppression, with associated risks of infection, malignancy, and drug toxicity, while chronic rejection remains a cause of late graft loss. Reliable tolerance would fundamentally change this care model by allowing sustained graft function without continuing drug exposure. Existing drug-free exceptions demonstrate that this goal is biologically possible, but do not make it broadly available.

The direct consequence would be removal of maintenance immunosuppression and its continuing treatment burden. Fewer drug complications, wider eligibility for patients who cannot tolerate those drugs, and less immune-mediated late graft loss are plausible benefits that require clinical demonstration. Their magnitude would depend on the toxicity of tolerance induction, patient selection, and durability of graft acceptance; replacing chronic drug toxicity with a hazardous conditioning procedure could diminish or erase the benefit.

The long-term ambition is durable acceptance across kidney, liver, heart, lung, and vascularized composite grafts. A successful kidney study plus a demonstration in one non-renal organ would establish an important extension, but would not establish lifelong acceptance across all those graft types. Tolerance would also leave other causes of failure, including recurrent disease, unresolved. The supplied reports of treatment resumption for recurrent disease illustrate this boundary.

missing_breakthrough.text: The unsolved capability is safe, durable, donor-specific acceptance across clinically important donor mismatches and transplantation settings. The supplied evidence establishes selected kidney successes, but does not establish routine tolerance for mismatched deceased-donor grafts or human transplantation across non-renal organs. Conditioning toxicity, inconsistent success across HLA barriers, and late donor-specific antibody development remain central obstacles.

Deceased-donor transplantation creates a timing problem for several combined kidney–bone-marrow protocols because conditioning must begin days before transplantation. This limitation is protocol-specific: the supplied review describes Stanford conditioning that can begin after transplantation and could therefore have deceased-donor applicability. However, its demonstrated sustained drug-free success has principally involved fully HLA-matched recipients. Solving scheduling alone would not solve the mismatch barrier. Delayed tolerance, induced after an organ has already been transplanted, is another route under investigation.

Chimerism-based approaches must balance immune reprogramming against injury from conditioning and donor immune cells. The initial Massachusetts General Hospital regimen frequently caused chimerism-transition syndrome with acute kidney injury, although the supplied review reports that later protocol iterations avoided this complication. Full donor chimerism offers another route to prolonged drug-free acceptance in mismatched recipients, but retains graft-versus-host disease risk; facilitating cells reduce rather than eliminate that risk. More durable tolerance must also withstand late antibody responses without requiring renewed immunosuppression.

Cross-organ extension requires evidence beyond kidney protocols. The supplied review describes nonhuman-primate lung and liver work, but that supports further investigation rather than a conclusion that the same regimen will work safely in human recipients of those organs. The liver extension is attributed to a manuscript in submission, adding a publication and verification limitation.

current_state.text: The 2026 review by Wilson and colleagues reports that, among 10 recipients in the initial Massachusetts General Hospital HLA-mismatched living-donor combined kidney–bone-marrow trial, seven achieved immunosuppression-free kidney graft survival for at least five years. Two remained off immunosuppression for more than 15 years with normal creatinine. Other recipients resumed treatment for donor-specific antibodies or recurrent disease. These are substantial clinical demonstrations in a selected living-donor kidney cohort, rather than evidence of general applicability to deceased donors or other organs.

The reconciled research separately attributes publication-specific results to the 2014 Kawai report: transient chimerism in all 10 recipients, immunosuppression withdrawal lasting at least four years in seven, four still off drugs for 4.5–11.4 years at publication, and three allograft failures. The source index contains no captured text for that article, so these details cannot be independently assessed from the supplied review materials. They remain attributed historical figures, not verified findings of this record. The 2026 review's later five-year summary does not independently establish the earlier publication's exact counts or follow-up ranges.

For the initial Massachusetts General Hospital regimen, the 2026 review reports chimerism-transition syndrome with acute kidney injury in 9 of 10 recipients and states that later protocol iterations avoided this complication. It also reports that none of 22 Stanford one-haplotype-matched recipients achieved immunosuppression-free kidney allograft survival. Together, these findings show why selected successes cannot be extrapolated across conditioning regimens and degrees of HLA matching.

The randomized phase 3 MDR-101 trial, published in 2025, studied adult kidney recipients with two-haplotype HLA-matched living-sibling donors. Its supplied abstract reports that 15 of 20 treatment recipients, or 75%, achieved more than two years without immunosuppression. Four resumed treatment: one for recurrent immunoglobulin A nephropathy, one for recurrent disease with rejection, one for rejection, and one for borderline biopsy changes. No deaths, graft losses, donor-specific antibodies, or graft-versus-host disease were reported in the treatment results. Access in the supplied review was to the abstract, not the full trial text; these results establish what that abstract reports and do not establish equivalent outcomes with mismatched deceased donors.

The 2026 review describes delayed tolerance in nonhuman primates, including lung work and liver work attributed to a manuscript in submission, as well as one fully HLA-matched living-donor kidney recipient treated at UCLA. It reports no deceased-donor clinical series. It also describes prolonged drug-free acceptance through full-chimerism approaches in mismatched recipients, with residual graft-versus-host disease risk. These distinct routes provide partial progress; none of these observations establishes broad, safe tolerance across deceased-donor transplantation and multiple human organs.

The evidence coverage is bounded by the supplied publications. The validated review assessed a complete retained narrative of the 2026 kidney-focused review and the MDR-101 abstract, while the 2014 article was not captured. No freshness searches were supplied, so the absence of a deceased-donor series in this review cannot be treated as a comprehensive finding that no such clinical report existed through November 1, 2026. The kidney-focused scope likewise limits conclusions about every non-renal approach.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: a multicenter study in HLA-mismatched deceased-donor kidney recipients, accompanied by a demonstration in at least one non-renal solid organ, should show that a prespecified majority can remain off all immunosuppression for more than two years. Graft survival and function should be comparable to contemporary controls receiving standard drugs. The majority threshold and two-year duration are proposed milestones, not established standards; a protocol would need an exact success threshold, numerical comparability margins, and enough participants to support the intended conclusions.
completion_criteria.label: Majority sustain drug-free kidney and non-renal grafts beyond two years

completion_criteria.text: Proposed safety and practicality requirements: the studies should observe no graft-versus-host disease and should show that conditioning-related mortality and morbidity do not cancel the benefit of drug withdrawal. Assessment should include acute organ injury, serious infections, recovery burden, treatment resumption, and feasibility within deceased-donor transplantation timelines. An absence of observed events in a finite cohort would bound demonstrated safety, rather than prove that the risks are zero.
completion_criteria.label: No graft-versus-host disease and net benefit from immunosuppression withdrawal

completion_criteria.text: Proposed durability and reproducibility requirements: independent centers should reproduce outcomes using a defined protocol, with a prespecified long-term surveillance schedule for graft function, rejection, donor-specific antibodies, and renewed immunosuppression. Follow-up should extend beyond the initial withdrawal endpoint to detect late failure. Evidence of preserved responses to unrelated antigens would strengthen the interpretation of donor-specific tolerance beyond the observation of drug-free function alone. These proposed assessments respond to the late antibody and durability problems described in the supplied review.
completion_criteria.label: Independent centers reproduce tolerance with surveillance beyond initial drug withdrawal

completion_criteria.text: Proposed scope boundary: successful kidney and one-organ results would demonstrate reproducible tolerance within the tested donor types, recipients, organs, and follow-up periods. Further studies would be needed for other organs, broader patient selection, and longer durability. No finite trial could establish literal universality or lifelong acceptance in every recipient.
completion_criteria.label: Tolerance claims remain limited to tested scope and follow-up

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: SUR-02, destination-therapy solid-organ xenotransplantation, shares the challenge of durable immune acceptance. SUR-01 concerns tolerance to human donor grafts; extending it to animal-derived organs would require additional cross-species solutions. Success in human allograft tolerance would therefore not establish destination xenotransplantation, and the supplied sources do not specify the additional xenograft requirements.

Roster-based synthesis: SUR-03, life-sustaining cryobanking of human-scale organs, addresses preservation and availability, whereas SUR-01 addresses recipient immune acceptance. The capabilities could complement one another: preservation could potentially provide more scheduling flexibility, but that possibility is not demonstrated by the supplied evidence. Cryobanking alone would not establish tolerance.

Roster-based synthesis: SUR-09, living, perfused autologous replacements for complex parts, and SUR-12, life-sustaining autologous solid organs assembled for implantation, address replacement through a patient's own biological material. Their overlap with SUR-01 is restoration of durable tissue or organ function. Their central challenge is constructing suitable replacements; SUR-01 instead seeks acceptance of donor tissue. Autologous origin would not by itself establish that an engineered replacement functions safely or durably.

Roster-based synthesis: SUR-04, restoration after complete spinal cord transection, and SUR-05, regenerative adult wound healing, concern functional repair and regeneration rather than donor-specific immune acceptance. SUR-06, autonomous whole operations, SUR-07, incisionless internal resection and reconstruction, SUR-10, cell-identity-selective extirpation, and SUR-11, cellular and molecular operative vision, concern how interventions are performed or guided. SUR-08, reversible metabolic arrest after traumatic exsanguination cardiac arrest, concerns emergency preservation and resuscitation. These remain distinct innovations even where they might eventually assist transplantation or reconstructive care.

change_log.change: Defined operational drug-free acceptance separately from proven lifelong donor-specific immune tolerance.
change_log.reason: Observed graft function without drugs does not by itself establish lifelong durability or the full immune mechanism.

change_log.change: Replaced the universal claim that functioning transplants always require continuous immunosuppression with a general baseline that acknowledges selected exceptions.
change_log.reason: The supplied evidence documents prolonged drug-free graft acceptance.

change_log.change: Made the pre-transplant conditioning barrier protocol-specific and included Stanford's post-transplant conditioning exception.
change_log.reason: The review does not support a blanket claim that all tolerance regimens require advance conditioning.

change_log.change: Removed the assertion that deceased-donor and non-renal operations account for most clinical need.
change_log.reason: The supplied material does not quantify that distribution; the core clinical gap remains without this assertion.

change_log.change: Integrated the later Massachusetts General Hospital outcomes, initial 9-of-10 acute kidney injury complication, later avoidance of that complication, and Stanford's 22-recipient mismatched cohort.
change_log.reason: These details preserve both the clinical proof of principle and the regimen-specific barriers identified by the review.

change_log.change: Retained the research's 2014 quantitative details only as explicitly unverified historical attributions.
change_log.reason: The article was not captured, and the later review cannot verify publication-specific figures. Lack of retained evidence does not establish that the figures are false.

change_log.change: Specified the MDR-101 population, 15-of-20 endpoint result, four treatment resumptions and their causes, and abstract-only access.
change_log.reason: These details explain the demonstrated achievement while preventing extrapolation to mismatched deceased donors.

change_log.change: Distinguished nonhuman-primate findings, a liver manuscript in submission, the single matched UCLA case, and full-chimerism approaches.
change_log.reason: These represent different levels and routes of progress, with different limits and safety implications.

change_log.change: Qualified broader eligibility, reduced late graft loss, cross-organ applicability, and lifelong acceptance as conditional outcomes.
change_log.reason: These benefits exceed what the reported cohorts and proposed two-year milestone establish; recurrent disease and other causes of graft failure remain.

change_log.change: Expanded the proposed completion demonstration to address numerical margins, conditioning morbidity, reproducibility, long-term surveillance, and finite-test limits.
change_log.reason: A convincing clinical milestone needs defined efficacy, safety, durability, and scope without presenting proposed thresholds as authoritative standards.

change_log.change: Bounded evidence coverage to the supplied publications and preserved source-access limitations.
change_log.reason: No freshness searches establish comprehensive coverage through November 1, 2026, and the principal review is kidney-focused.

unresolved_issues: The exact 2014 publication-specific counts, follow-up ranges, transient-chimerism result, and three reported graft failures remain unverified from retained source text. The review recommendation to remove these figures was not adopted literally because the task requests preservation of unresolved quantitative detail; they are retained only as qualified research attributions.
The supplied materials do not establish comprehensive literature coverage through November 1, 2026. Whether additional deceased-donor or non-renal clinical results existed by that date remains open.
The liver delayed-tolerance work is described through a review's reference to a manuscript in submission; its primary methods and results were not available in the supplied evidence.
The MDR-101 evidence available to the review is an abstract. Full protocol details and longer-term outcomes cannot be inferred from that access.
Exact efficacy thresholds, comparability margins, acceptable conditioning morbidity, cohort sizes, and long-term surveillance intervals remain to be specified for the proposed demonstration.
The durability, patient-selection boundaries, cross-organ transferability, and net clinical benefit of a broadly applicable tolerance protocol remain unresolved.

brief.title: Organ transplants without lifelong anti-rejection drugs
possible: People could receive a donated organ and keep it working without ongoing drugs that suppress the immune system. Their immune system would accept the organ while still defending against unrelated threats.

This could become reliable for organs from deceased donors, donors whose immune markers differ from the recipient’s, and organs beyond kidneys. The treatment that establishes acceptance would also have to be acceptably safe.
why: Transplant recipients would lose the continuing burden of anti-rejection treatment. Avoiding these drugs could reduce infections, cancer and damage caused by the drugs themselves.
More people who cannot tolerate these medicines could become eligible for transplantation. Preventing the immune system from slowly damaging the donated organ could also help transplants last longer.

sources.showed: This clinical report follows recipients of combined kidney and bone marrow transplants from living donors with differing immune markers after withdrawal of ongoing anti-rejection drugs.
sources.cited_for: It supports the possibility of lasting kidney acceptance without ongoing anti-rejection drugs despite differences in donor immune markers.
sources.not_established: Selected living-donor kidney results do not establish safe, reliable acceptance of deceased-donor organs or other organ types.

sources.who: Avery Wilson and colleagues at Massachusetts General Hospital
sources.showed: Their review describes lasting drug-free kidney acceptance using donor blood-forming cells to reshape the recipient’s immune system. Success varied with donor matching and treatment, and some approaches caused serious harm.
sources.quote: Over the past two decades, through various strategies and conditioning regimens, renal allograft tolerance has been achieved in humans.
sources.cited_for: It supports both the biological possibility of drug-free acceptance and the remaining barriers of safety, donor matching and durability.
sources.not_established: The reviewed successes do not establish broadly safe acceptance across deceased donors and multiple human organ types.

sources.who: Dixon B Kaufman and the MDR-101-MLK Study Group
sources.showed: In a randomized trial, 75% of treated recipients met the goal of sustained freedom from anti-rejection drugs. All received kidneys from living siblings with closely matched immune markers.
sources.quote: Twenty recipients received the MDR-101 infusion, and none developed graft versus host disease.
sources.cited_for: It demonstrates sustained drug-free kidney acceptance in a randomized trial of closely matched living-sibling transplants.
sources.not_established: These results do not establish equivalent success with mismatched deceased donors, other organs or lifelong follow-up.

shown: At Massachusetts General Hospital, selected recipients of living-donor kidneys with differing immune markers achieved prolonged acceptance without ongoing drugs. Some remained off treatment for more than 15 years with normal kidney function.

The MDR-101 trial extended drug-free kidney acceptance to a randomized study across hospitals, using closely matched living-sibling donors. Some recipients restarted treatment because of rejection, recurrent disease or concerning biopsy findings.
missing: Reliable drug-free acceptance still needs demonstration for kidneys from deceased donors whose immune markers differ from the recipient’s.
Human studies must establish safe drug-free acceptance in organs beyond kidneys.
Preparatory treatment must avoid serious harm and fit the unpredictable timing of deceased-donor transplantation.
Long-term acceptance must withstand late immune attacks while preserving useful defenses against unrelated threats.

milestones.label: Most recipients sustain drug-free kidney and other organ transplants
milestones.explanation: A multicenter study of mismatched deceased-donor kidneys, plus another solid organ, would have to show a majority drug-free beyond two years with function and survival comparable to standard care. This would establish broader usefulness.

milestones.label: Drug withdrawal brings net benefit without donor-cell attacks
milestones.explanation: Studies would have to observe no attacks on recipients by donor immune cells and show that treatment harms do not outweigh withdrawal benefits within deceased-donor timelines. This would establish safety and practicality.

milestones.label: Independent centers reproduce acceptance with continued monitoring
milestones.explanation: Independent centers would have to reproduce a defined protocol and monitor organ function, rejection, donor-targeting antibodies and restarted drugs beyond withdrawal. This would test durability; preserved unrelated defenses would strengthen it.

milestones.label: Claims stay within the patients and follow-up tested
milestones.explanation: Claims of success would have to stay within the donor types, recipients, organs and follow-up studied. Broader or lifelong acceptance would remain a separate question.

uncertain: The required success rate, acceptable treatment harm and margins for comparison with standard care remain to be defined.
It remains unclear which patients and organ types can achieve lasting acceptance with a shared treatment approach.
A working organ without drugs does not by itself prove lifelong acceptance or preserved immune defenses against unrelated threats.

page.title: Operational tolerance in deceased-donor organ transplantation
page.definition: A finite treatment enables a recipient to stop all maintenance anti-rejection drugs while an organ from a deceased donor continues to function. Donor and recipient differ at one or more human leukocyte antigens (HLA), the markers used for tissue matching. Operational tolerance describes observed drug-free graft function and can also arise spontaneously. Donor-specific tolerance additionally requires evidence that the recipient accepts the donor tissue and still responds to unrelated antigens.

goal.need: Deceased donors provided organs for 41,119 US transplants in 2024. Recipients generally need anti-rejection drugs for life. These drugs also weaken defenses against serious infections. Across 175,732 US solid-organ transplants in 1987–2008, cancer incidence was 2.10 times expected (95% CI 2.06–2.14). Safe tolerance induction could let recipients keep a functioning organ without years of drug toxicity. How much of the excess cancer risk withdrawal would prevent remains unknown.

completion.title: FDA approves a treatment for complete drug withdrawal after HLA-mismatched deceased-donor transplantation.
completion.criterion: For the organ in question, FDA grants marketing authorization for a treatment whose approved use includes planned withdrawal of all maintenance immunosuppression after HLA-mismatched deceased-donor transplantation while preserving graft function. For a product regulated as a licensed biologic, the authorization is a biologics license. The approved recipient population, regimen and monitoring requirements define the scope of the claim.
completion.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, its published intended-use approval criterion and 21 CFR 601.4(a) for biological products; applied separately to each organ indication.
completion.threshold_quote: a drug has been shown to be safe and effective for its intended use
completion.basis: US marketing authorization establishes that a particular treatment can be marketed for the specified use. An individual can meet the clinical definition of operational tolerance before such authorization. FDA assesses the proposed indication and its evidence without specifying a single drug-free duration or response fraction across organs.

milestones.title: A laboratory animal accepts donor grafts without drugs while retaining unrelated immune responses.
milestones.criterion: After a finite induction regimen, the animal accepts a donor graft without maintenance immunosuppression and retains immune responses to unrelated antigens. To establish this result for an organ case, demonstrate acceptance of that organ. Skin-graft acceptance establishes the tissue-model result.
milestones.set_by: Experimental transplantation convention, stated and historically documented by Wilson and colleagues; the early demonstrations used skin grafts.
milestones.threshold_quote: lack of a destructive, antigen-specific immune response to an allograft in the absence of immunosuppression

milestones.title: A nonhuman primate accepts an organ graft and passes a donor-specific skin-graft test.
milestones.criterion: After finite induction treatment, the primate maintains a functioning organ graft without maintenance immunosuppression. In a subsequent skin-graft challenge, it accepts skin from the organ donor while rejecting unrelated donor skin. For simultaneous organ transplants, identify the combination tested.
milestones.set_by: Experimental donor-specific skin-graft challenge used in rhesus kidney transplantation and in primate heart–kidney transplantation.

milestones.title: An organ recipient receives a tolerance-induction treatment in a phase 1 clinical study.
milestones.criterion: An organ recipient receives the investigational tolerance-induction treatment in an authorized phase 1 study or in the phase 1 component of a combined early-phase study, with initial safety observations.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 312.21(a), defining initial human investigation.
milestones.threshold_quote: initial introduction of an investigational new drug into humans.

milestones.title: An organ recipient maintains a rejection-free graft without immunosuppression for at least one year.
milestones.criterion: For at least one year after complete withdrawal of immunosuppressive drugs, the recipient maintains a functioning graft without histological signs of rejection and retains immune competence. Record whether withdrawal followed a planned tolerance-induction intervention, the donor type and the HLA match.
milestones.set_by: Clinical operational-tolerance convention described by Page, Dar and Knechtle.
milestones.threshold_quote: a well-functioning graft lacking histological signs of rejection, in the absence of any immunosuppressive drugs (for at least 1 year), in an immunocompetent host

milestones.title: Pivotal studies establish benefit and risk for withdrawal in HLA-mismatched deceased-donor recipients.
milestones.criterion: For the specified organ and HLA-mismatched deceased-donor population, pivotal studies meet their prespecified efficacy tests for planned complete withdrawal with maintained graft function. Safety and efficacy data permit assessment of the overall benefit–risk relationship for the proposed labeling.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 312.21(c), applied to the proposed indication.
milestones.threshold_quote: evaluate the overall benefit-risk relationship of the drug

milestones.title: A controlled study shows preliminary efficacy in HLA-mismatched deceased-donor recipients.
milestones.criterion: For the organ studied, a controlled clinical investigation in HLA-mismatched deceased-donor recipients provides preliminary evidence that planned complete withdrawal can preserve graft function and characterizes common short-term side effects and risks. Evaluate efficacy against the study’s prespecified endpoint and follow-up interval.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 312.21(b)–(c), defining the purpose of phase 2 and the evidence preceding phase 3, applied to the intended organ and donor population.
milestones.threshold_quote: preliminary evidence suggesting effectiveness of the drug has been obtained

not_found: No published cross-organ success fraction, follow-up duration or acceptable conditioning-risk limit was found in the NIAID goals, ITN strategy, FDA criteria or examined trial records.
No pivotal efficacy result establishing induced tolerance in HLA-mismatched deceased-donor recipients was located for the listed organs.
ClinicalTrials.gov records did not render their study details; sponsor-submitted text was readable through the ICH GCP mirror.
The full text of the Salzburg liver cell-therapy recommendations published on 28 October 2026 was paywalled.

No human heart-transplant report was found documenting planned tolerance induction followed by a full year off immunosuppression with functioning, histologically rejection-free graft tissue and preserved immune competence.

results.finding: Of 20 MDR-101 recipients of HLA-matched living-sibling kidneys, 15 remained off immunosuppression for more than two years.
results.detail: Withdrawal was guided by donor mixed chimerism. Four recipients restarted immunosuppression. Two had rejection, one had recurrent IgA nephropathy alone, and one had borderline biopsy changes.
results.quote: Fifteen (75%) reached the primary study endpoint of IS-free for >2 years.

results.finding: In a 30-recipient randomized kidney trial, 75% of MDR-101 recipients reached the drug-free endpoint.
results.detail: The abstract reports reasons for restarting immunosuppression and the absence of graft-versus-host disease. It gives no comprehensive short-term adverse-event profile.
results.quote: Fifteen (75%) reached the primary study endpoint of IS-free for >2 years.

results.finding: In a 30-recipient phase 3 kidney trial, 75% of MDR-101 recipients reached the primary drug-free endpoint.
results.quote: Fifteen (75%) reached the primary study endpoint of IS-free for >2 years.

results.finding: Among 6 treated rhesus kidney recipients, 3 maintained graft function without maintenance immunosuppression. Third-party responsiveness was documented in a survivor.

results.finding: One bilateral lung transplant recipient maintained a functioning, rejection-free graft for more than 3 years after complete immunosuppression withdrawal.

results.quote: She has been attending college, running 5k races, and has been free from immunosuppression for more than 3 years.

definition = "A finite treatment enables a recipient to stop all maintenance anti-rejection drugs while an organ from a deceased donor continues to function. Donor and recipient differ at one or more human leukocyte antigens (HLA), the markers used for tissue matching. Operational tolerance describes observed drug-free graft function and can also arise spontaneously. Donor-specific tolerance additionally requires evidence that the recipient accepts the donor tissue and still responds to unrelated antigens.". Reason: The definition needs to distinguish planned induction from spontaneous drug-free function and explain what is mismatched.

goal.need = "Deceased donors provided organs for 41,119 US transplants in 2024. Recipients generally need anti-rejection drugs for life. These drugs also weaken defenses against serious infections. Across 175,732 US solid-organ transplants in 1987\u20132008, cancer incidence was 2.10 times expected (95% CI 2.06\u20132.14). Safe tolerance induction could let recipients keep a functioning organ without years of drug toxicity. How much of the excess cancer risk withdrawal would prevent remains unknown.". Reason: The current rationale names a research programme where readers need the scale of deceased donation, the burden of continuing treatment and the limits of the cancer estimate.

add statement by European Medicines Agency, Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use, 2008: "to introduce new concepts of treatment (such as tolerance induction and exclusion of maintenance therapy) replacing well-established concepts". Reason: The European regulator’s adopted guideline explicitly identifies elimination of maintenance therapy through tolerance induction as a treatment-development goal.

edit completion: title = "FDA approves a treatment for complete drug withdrawal after HLA-mismatched deceased-donor transplantation."; criterion = "For the organ in question, FDA grants marketing authorization for a treatment whose approved use includes planned withdrawal of all maintenance immunosuppression after HLA-mismatched deceased-donor transplantation while preserving graft function. For a product regulated as a licensed biologic, the authorization is a biologics license. The approved recipient population, regimen and monitoring requirements define the scope of the claim."; basis = "US marketing authorization establishes that a particular treatment can be marketed for the specified use. An individual can meet the clinical definition of operational tolerance before such authorization. FDA assesses the proposed indication and its evidence without specifying a single drug-free duration or response fraction across organs."; refs = [6, 7, 8, 13, 24]. Reason: FDA approves a treatment for a labeled use, and the existing title could be read as requiring FDA permission for an individual recipient to stop a drug.
add case "Intestine". Reason: NIAID names intestine as a distinct organ model in its tolerance programme.

edit m1: criterion = "After a finite induction regimen, the animal accepts a donor graft without maintenance immunosuppression and retains immune responses to unrelated antigens. To establish this result for an organ case, demonstrate acceptance of that organ. Skin-graft acceptance establishes the tissue-model result.". Reason: The current criterion mixes the experimental test with a historical account that omits the earlier fetal-mouse demonstration.

edit m2: criterion = "After finite induction treatment, the primate maintains a functioning organ graft without maintenance immunosuppression. In a subsequent skin-graft challenge, it accepts skin from the organ donor while rejecting unrelated donor skin. For simultaneous organ transplants, identify the combination tested."; set_by = "Experimental donor-specific skin-graft challenge used in rhesus kidney transplantation and in primate heart\u2013kidney transplantation."; threshold_quote = "tolerance confirmed by skin grafting"; threshold_ref = 10; refs = [10, 19]. Reason: The primate criterion embeds a kidney study’s result and leaves readers to infer what a donor-specific skin challenge tests.

edit m3: criterion = "An organ recipient receives the investigational tolerance-induction treatment in an authorized phase 1 study or in the phase 1 component of a combined early-phase study, with initial safety observations."; set_by = "US Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 312.21(a), defining initial human investigation."; refs = [11, 12, 25]. Reason: The phase 1 criterion includes study sizes and safety findings that belong with the results, and its attribution unnecessarily restricts the clinical examples to two organs.

edit m4: criterion = "For at least one year after complete withdrawal of immunosuppressive drugs, the recipient maintains a functioning graft without histological signs of rejection and retains immune competence. Record whether withdrawal followed a planned tolerance-induction intervention, the donor type and the HLA match."; set_by = "Clinical operational-tolerance convention described by Page, Dar and Knechtle."; refs = [13, 9, 12, 24, 30]. Reason: The one-year test is sound, but its criterion contains trial outcomes and its attribution overlooks the deceased-donor lung evidence.

add milestone after m4: "A controlled study shows preliminary efficacy in HLA-mismatched deceased-donor recipients.". Reason: An individual drug-free recipient and a pivotal trial leave a gap for controlled evidence of preliminary efficacy and short-term risk in the intended deceased-donor population.

edit m5: title = "Pivotal studies establish benefit and risk for withdrawal in HLA-mismatched deceased-donor recipients."; criterion = "For the specified organ and HLA-mismatched deceased-donor population, pivotal studies meet their prespecified efficacy tests for planned complete withdrawal with maintained graft function. Safety and efficacy data permit assessment of the overall benefit\u2013risk relationship for the proposed labeling."; set_by = "US Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 312.21(c), applied to the proposed indication."; threshold_quote = "evaluate the overall benefit-risk relationship of the drug"; threshold_ref = 11; refs = [11, 6]. Reason: The pivotal criterion gives a matched living-donor trial’s endpoint and outcome more prominence than the population for which efficacy must be established.
